artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: New helper group_canonical_bronze_keys(prefix, keys): groups sorted keys by (partition, report_id), the first-seen key per group is the canonical one (keys arrive sorted from the caller, so first-seen IS lexicographically first). _run_write and _run_v2 now iterate canonical_keys only (not every listed key), print one duplicate-content line per skip (_print_duplicates) and add a duplicates <n> field to their summary print. New --duplicates CLI mode (_run_duplicates): read-only, no store write, prints 'objects <n> report_ids <m> duplicates <d>' then one duplicate-content line per pair.

_run_write now imports lib.research.corpus.extract and calls its group_canonical_bronze_keys on the sorted bronze key list before the per-object loop, prints the same duplicate-content lines via extract_mod._print_duplicates, and iterates canonical_keys only -- one typed row per report_id, from the canonical (bronze_key/extract_key) pair. Summary line now reads 'silver_rows %d of %d bronze duplicates %d'.

New file, offline, a stub S3 client (same shape as test_ingest.py's _FakeS3Client, never real boto3). 7 tests: the grouping helper picks the lexicographic first key and is identity on a no-duplicate corpus; extract._run_write puts exactly one extract.json for a duplicate pair and prints duplicate-content + 'duplicates 1'; extract._run_write on a no-duplicate corpus prints 'duplicates 0' and stores one object per object (today's behaviour, unaffected shape); extract._run_duplicates writes nothing and prints the exact 'objects <n> report_ids <m> duplicates <d>' + duplicate-content line shape; main() routes --duplicates to _run_duplicates; typed._run_write emits exactly one silver row (from the canonical key's bronze_key) for the duplicate pair and prints the same duplicate-content line. All 7 pass.
